messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident triggered: HIGH latency SLO breach on /v1/generate (p99 = 2.3s, threshold=1.2s). Alert group: inference-prod-eu. PD:INC-98127 link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-98127 :rotating_light:
Aisha Patel: acked PD. I'm on it. Starting triage — pulling recent deploys and autoscaler events.
Marco Diaz: I saw an uptick in KV-cache miss ratio in the last 5m, could be a cache eviction storm. Pulling metrics: https://grafana.redwood/d/latency/inference-prod
Riley Chen: Reindexing didn't happen, right? No DB ops. I can check model rollout history.
Jun Park: I noticed a canary for model v2.3 rolled out 11m ago on eu-west. P95 jump coincides. Opening rollout history: /console/rollouts/rollout-7332
Leah Ortiz: Support is getting multiple customer complaints about slow responses in EU. Triage priority: customer-facing apps degraded.
Aisha Patel: Quick plan — 1) pause rollout and switch traffic to v2.2 variant, 2) bump pool capacity for eu-west dedicated nodes by +2, 3) enable fallback routing to cheaper replica. Who can flip the rollout?
Marco Diaz: I can pause the rollout. Command: `redwood rollout pause rollout-7332 --env=prod --region=eu-west`
Riley Chen: I'm on the autoscaler. Increasing desired nodes: `rgctl scale --pool inference-eu-west --add 2`
incident-bot: Executing action: rollout pause requested by Marco Diaz.
pagerduty: Incident INC-98127 acknowledged by Aisha Patel at 2468101360. Escalation hold set to 15m.
Marco Diaz: Rollout pause succeeded. Traffic should be shifting to v2.2 within the next 30s.
Aisha Patel: Observability: p99 dropped from 2.3s to 1.9s after pause, still above SLO. Working with Riley on autoscale.
Riley Chen: Scale command applied; new nodes provisioning. Also saw an autoscale cooldown misconfig set to 10m earlier — changed to 60s for faster reaction.
Jun Park: Looking at KV cache logs — eviction rate spiked due to a misconfigured prefix in v2.3 serving path. That would amplify tail latency. Root cause likely rollout path.
Leah Ortiz: Notifying affected accounts: Drafting short status update to customers impacted in EU. ETA for mitigation ~10-15m.
Aisha Patel: Can we temporarily enable prefix caching on proxies to reduce miss penalty? Marco, can you push proxy config: `infractl apply -f proxy-cache-temporary.yaml`
Marco Diaz: Applying now. `kubectl apply -f proxy-cache-temporary.yaml -n inference-prod`
incident-bot: Config change detected; proxy cache TTL increased.
Aisha Patel: Good, p99 down to 1.1s now. Under SLO threshold. Reassessing.
Riley Chen: New nodes are up but not needed anymore since traffic back to good variant. I'll scale back one node to be safe.
Jun Park: I'll escalate with model-onboarding to prevent that rollout from auto-retrying. Adding a hold and a rollback to staging.
Leah Ortiz: Sent customer update: "We've mitigated the latency spike by reverting a recent model rollout and applying a temporary proxy cache. We're monitoring. We'll follow up with a post-incident note."
Aisha Patel: Great job. Next steps: create a short postmortem, include root cause (rollout introduced cache key change), action items: 1) add rollout gating test for cache key invariants, 2) fix autoscale cooldown default, 3) add synthetic p99 probe for eu-west. I'll create incident oncall ticket and assign.
Marco Diaz: Logging runbook link here: https://confluence.redwood/runbooks/latency-slo-breach. Adding checklist items.
Riley Chen: Handing off to follow-up SREs for postmortem. Oncall next shift: Jun.
Jun Park: Acknowledged handoff. I'll take ownership for the postmortem and customer follow-ups.
Aisha Patel: Closing PD incident; setting incident to resolved in 5m unless it flares. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
